title: Palamas and the uncreated light
hookLine: on Mount Athos, monks praying the Jesus Prayer say they see the light of Tabor
last: THE LOVE THAT MOVES THE SUN.

cards: Night on Mount Athos, a rocky peninsula in Greece, home to monks. In a small cell, a monk sits on a low stool, head bowed, breathing slowly.
With each breath he says the same short prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me. Hours go by. And some of these monks say that in the stillness they see light.
Not a lamp, not the moon: a light they say is God's own, the same light the disciples saw on Mount Tabor. Others laughed at them. Today's word is what the monks were doing.

teach.b: Hesychasm. When Paul tells one church, in the King James Bible, to "study to be quiet," the Greek verb he uses is from the same family: hesychazo, to be still. Hesychasts are the people of stillness.

teach.h: HAVE MERCY ON ME, WITH THE BREATH.
teach.b: Their prayer, the Jesus Prayer, grows out of cries in the Gospels: the tax collector's "God be merciful to me a sinner," and the blind man's "Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me." Said slowly, with the breath.
And the light? They point to the Transfiguration.

teach.h: WHITE AS THE LIGHT ON TABOR.
teach.b: Jesus takes three disciples up a mountain, tradition says Tabor, and there, Matthew writes, "his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light." The monks say that light can still be seen.
A learned man named Barlaam mocked them: God can't be seen with bodily eyes, so whatever you're seeing, it isn't God. A monk of Athos, Gregory Palamas, answered with a distinction.
God's essence, what God is in himself, is beyond every creature, forever. But God's energies, his life, his grace, his light, are truly God too, uncreated, and God gives them.
So a person can really share in God's light without swallowing up God's mystery. Church councils in Constantinople sided with Palamas, and Orthodox Christians honor him as a saint.
Western churches have read his ideas in different ways, and theologians still discuss them. For the people of stillness, the quiet was never empty. It was a cell kept ready for light.

how: Orthodox Christians, and some Catholics and Protestants, pray the Jesus Prayer, often with a prayer rope, and Orthodox churches keep a Sunday in Lent in memory of Gregory Palamas.

games.q: you're Gregory Palamas. a learned man says the monks of Athos can't be seeing God's light, because God can't be seen. how do you answer?
o: agree, and tell the monks to stop.
say God's essence is beyond us, but God's energies, his light, are truly God and truly given.
say the monks see God's essence directly.
games.why: Palamas distinguishes God's essence, beyond every creature, from God's energies, uncreated and truly shared. councils in Constantinople sided with him.

practice: If you can, dim the room and light a candle, a small lamp, or even a blank white screen, and let your eyes rest on it without staring hard, breathing slowly in and out.
If you pray, you can say the old prayer of the monks with the breath, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me; if not, let the breath be the prayer and the light be enough.

wordCard.voice: Hesychasm. Stillness: a way of prayer from the Christian East, the Jesus Prayer said with the breath, defended by Gregory Palamas.

orig.note: Greek: stillness, quiet. the stillness the hesychasts sought in prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: the light of tabor. Seven days, from Elizabeth's bread to a cell on Athos. A week closes: day eight hundred twenty-six.
